# The appointments Kérberos made — and who is keeping them

The mistake is reading myths as entertainment. Kérberos's cycle reads more like a charter — each story assigning a duty the modern world still pays for.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Kérberos
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Domain of influence:** Underworld Guardian
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Technology & Innovation · Commerce & Governance · Home & Lifestyle
- **Strongest seat:** Cybersecurity & Digital Protection
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 83 of 449

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Cybersecurity & Digital Protection — through *Born of Typhon and Echidna*

Hesiod sets him in the monstrous brood of Typhon and Echidna (Theogony 306-312): Orthrus the hound of Geryon, then "Cerberus the flesh-eater, the brazen-voiced hound of Hades, fifty-headed, shameless and strong," and after him the Lernaean Hydra and the Chimaira.  The family is the underworld's kennel and armory in one: wherever the myths need an impossible guardian, one of Echidna's children is already on duty.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The three-headed watchdog at the gate; the perimeter that never sleeps.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Defense, Military & Security — through *The Porter of the Dead*

Later in the same poem (Theogony 767-773) Hesiod gives the hound his job description: he waits before the houses of Hades and dread Persephone, and on those who come in he fawns with his tail and both ears — but he lets none go back out; he watches, and devours whomsoever he catches passing the gates.  It is the earliest full portrait of the boundary's one-way logic: courtesy inward, annihilation outward.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The warden of the dead; border security with three heads and one rule — none leave.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Pet Care & Animal Industries — through *The Twelfth Labor*

The last and hardest labor set by Eurystheus was to bring the hound up from the dead.  Apollodorus (Library 2.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The most famous hound in myth; the ancestor of every guard dog.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Kérberos' myths are the myths of every threshold that must not be crossed — and of the handful of heroes who crossed his anyway.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

Skeptical? Good — the system is built for you. Every seat in this file carries its why-line and its weight, the full derivation is public at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/), and the challenge process is part of the design. Falsifiable is not a posture here; it is the mechanism.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in cybersecurity & digital protection, defense, military & security, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/cerberus/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
